description: Meet the "Row-bot," a robot that cleans up pollution and generates the electricity needed to power itself by swallowing dirty water. Roboticist Jonathan Rossiter explains how this special swimming machine, which uses a microbial fuel cell to neutralize algal blooms and oil slicks, could be a precursor to biodegradable, autonomous pollution-fighting robots. Hosted on Acast. See acast.com/privacy for more information.
classificationReason: Dedicated discussion of a pollution-eating autonomous robot, including its microbial fuel cell, swimming design, and potential applications.
qualityReason: Focused explanatory talk with a clear mechanism for the pollution-eating robot, concrete microbial-fuel-cell power figures, operating cycle, constraints, biodegradability, and deployment implications.
